title: Tiered Foreign Manpower and Levy Thresholds for Hawkers and Small F&B Operators
what_it_is: Tiered Foreign Manpower and Levy Thresholds for Hawkers and Small F&B Operators

sections.label: Hawker stallholder citizenship rules
sections.summary: MSE allows only Singaporean Citizens and Permanent Residents to be stallholders at hawker centres, while licensed food shops can hire foreign workers under levy rates and a two-locals-to-one-foreign-worker quota.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: To preserve the local identity of our hawker culture and heritage, the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) only allows Singaporean Citizens and Permanent Residents to be stallholders at our hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Licensed food shops, such as restaurants, can hire foreign workers, subject to the services foreign worker levy rates and quota of two locals to one foreign worker.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Differentiating levies and quotas further to favour smaller operators could incentivise the larger operators to break up into smaller entities to hire more foreign workers.

sections.label: Support schemes for small F&B
sections.summary: The Government has schemes supporting small F&B companies, including the FoodX programme for outsourcing food preparation to central kitchens and the F&B Process Optimisation Programme for technology adoption and process redesign.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: So, instead of just looking at raising headcounts, the Government has schemes to support small F&B companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: These include the FoodX programme, which supports the outsourcing of labour-intensive food preparation to central kitchens to improve operational efficiency; as well as the F&B Process Optimisation Programme, which supports technological adoption and process redesign.

sections.label: Headcount, authenticity and productivity trade-offs
sections.summary: The Government is prepared to consider more headcount if it makes sense, but that could impact recipe authenticity, and smaller operators may need to rethink business models and use government resources to be more productive.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If it makes sense for us to give them more headcount just to produce the food at a certain productivity level and maybe even quantity and efficiency, that is something we are prepared to consider.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But that will mean that the authenticity of the recipe could be impacted – that hawkers are selling a particular ethnic dish that is now not even cooked by the actual ethnicity, for example.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And if that is something that the broader Singaporean public can accept, that is conversation we should have and then decide how best to move forward on this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And in the end, smaller operators may really also have to rethink their business model and see how they can be more productive so that they are not going just by headcount.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: See how they can leverage on the rest of the resources the Government has put forth – Productivity Solutions Grant, working with central kitchen, for example – so that some of the backend operations that are very labour-intensive can be outsourced, while they focus on actually preparing the meals, making sure that it is authentic.
